sections.h2: What hospital bed management software does
paras: Hospital bed management software keeps one live picture of bed occupancy across the hospital, so that admission, transfer and discharge all update the same board. In HIMS the board is part of the inpatient workflow: a bed is allocated when the admission is raised, moved when the patient is transferred, and released when the discharge is completed, and the free-bed count feeds the hospital dashboard.

The board is organised by ward and bed type, general ward, private room, ICU and so on, so the admissions desk can answer a family or a referring doctor without phoning the ward. Because the bed belongs to an admission, room charges post to the IP bill for the days actually occupied.

sections.eyebrow: Why a bed register is not enough
sections.h2: The ward knows, the front desk guesses, the patient waits on a trolley.
sections.lead: Bed occupancy changes every hour. A register updated at the end of a shift is always wrong.

items.p: The front desk allots a bed from yesterday's register while the ward filled it from casualty overnight.
A patient moved from ICU to the ward is still shown in ICU, so the ICU looks full and the ward looks empty.
The patient left at noon; the bed is marked free at the evening handover, after a new admission was turned away.
Nobody is sure whether the patient was in the private room for three days or four, so the bill is argued at discharge.
Management asks how many beds are free right now, and the answer is a round of phone calls to each ward.

steps.p: Admissions desk sees free beds by ward and type on the board.
The bed is tied to the admission and shows as occupied for everyone.
Ward to ICU, or ICU step-down to the ward, moves the patient and both beds update.
Room and bed charges accrue to the IP bill for each bed and day.
Discharge frees the bed, and the dashboard count changes at once.

items.q: Is bed management a separate module?
items.a: It is part of the HIMS inpatient workflow. Beds are allocated when an admission is raised and released when the discharge completes, so the board stays current without a separate register. See IPD software.

items.q: Can we set up our own wards and bed types?
items.a: Yes. Wards, room categories and the beds in each are configured to match your building during setup, so the board looks like your hospital rather than a generic layout.

items.q: How do transfers between wards work?
items.a: A transfer moves the admission from one bed to another. The old bed becomes free and the new bed becomes occupied in the same action, and room charges change from the date of transfer.

items.q: Does the ICU appear on the same board?
items.a: Yes. ICU beds are part of the board and step-up or step-down moves are ordinary transfers. The ICU module also shows live vitals per bed. See ICU management software.

items.q: How does housekeeping know a bed is free?
items.a: The bed shows as released on the board the moment the discharge completes, so the ward and housekeeping can turn it around before the next admission is allocated. How the ward team coordinates the cleaning itself stays with your process.

items.q: Can management see occupancy without logging into the ward screen?
items.a: Yes. The hospital dashboard in HIMS shows OP, IP, beds and collections together, so occupied and free beds by ward are visible alongside the day's numbers.
